- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >72.5), model often overshoots downward in next 5–10 days — cap forecast decline to 1–2% below peak or align with 3–5 day moving average.
- If sentiment swings from negative to positive (e.g., -0.5 → +0.3), model frequently underreacts — increase forecast slope or add 0.5–1.0 point upward bias in first 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 10-day mean, reduce by 0.5–1.0 point; if below, add 0.5–1.0 point — especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward trends in bearish sentiment — add 0.5–1.5 point upward bias if sentiment < -0.3 for 5+ days.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — if sentiment jumps from -0.2 to -0.8, don’t assume 3–5 day collapse — model should adjust gradually, not jump 3–5 points down.
